subject: SIG & ISO intake — prioritized artifact lanes and secure upload cadence
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@highlandcap.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@highlandcap.com
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Highland Capital RFP — SIG/ISO evidence lane and upload cadence

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking the intake on short notice. The procurement and security teams at Highland need a practical plan for consuming SIG questionnaire responses alongside ISO 27001 artifact samples (scope: production, control plane, and SSO/KMS). Our timeline is tight — we need an initial evidence package and control crosswalk within 10 business days and ability to accept incremental artifact uploads thereafter.

Specific asks:
- A prioritized list of artifacts you will provide first (e.g., SOC 2 evidence, ISO scope map, KMS proof).
- Preferred secure upload mechanism (S3 presigned vs. portal upload vs. Drive link) and any required pre-signed TTLs / encryption expectations.
- A single point-of-contact at Redwood for artifact questions and an escalation contact for any gaps discovered during review.

We expect to validate: access control screenshots, key rotation logs (sample), change control tickets, and evidence of monitoring/telemetry for ingestion. Can you confirm what you can deliver in the first 10 business days and propose the phased cadence after that?

Appreciate a clear checklist we can align to.

Best,
Anya
Head of Vendor Assurance — Highland Capital

Attachment: Highland_SIG_Request_2029-06.pdf (reference only)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@highlandcap.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Highland Capital RFP — SIG/ISO evidence lane and upload cadence

Anya — thanks for the clear asks. High level plan below; attached is a worksheet (SIG_artifact_worksheet_v1.xlsx) with owners and a phased intake cadence.

What we can commit to in the first 10 business days (Phase 1):
- Completed SIG control crosswalk (CSV + summary) mapping Redwood controls to your SIG matrix.
- ISO 27001 scope map (pdf) showing included systems and boundary definitions.
- Sample artifacts: two KMS key rotation entries (redacted), one incident tabletop report, and a short telemetry runbook excerpt.

Phase 2 (days 11–30):
- Expanded artifact set for SOC 2 common criteria (config snapshots, access reviews) and additional KMS proof points.
- Live walkthrough (30–45 mins) for your assurance team on how Redwood stores audit logs and how customers can request exports.

Secure upload preference: we prefer S3 presigned uploads into a hardened bucket in our assurance workspace with object-level encryption. Details:
- Presigned URLs will expire after 72 hours by default; we can extend to 7 days on a per-file basis if required.
- Objects are encrypted with SSE-KMS (Redwood-managed key); we will provide a sample key proof JSON for your review.
- We will also provide a temporary (timeboxed) link to a Drive folder for docs that cannot be presigned (e.g., screenshots).

Single point-of-contact: this mailbox (priyom_das@redwood.com) for day-to-day artifact intake. Escalation: kimberly_park@redwood.com (Security Program Lead) for technical exceptions and marissa_cole@redwood.com for contract-level issues.

Next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance of S3 presigned flow and desired presign TTL.
2) I'll drop the Phase 1 worksheet into the folder and share the first presigned upload endpoints once confirmed.
3) Propose a short kickoff call tomorrow morning (30 mins) to walk owners through the worksheet.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Assurance Program Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG_artifact_worksheet_v1.xlsx; ISO_scope_map_v2.pdf; S3_upload_instructions.txt
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Highland cap — owners and evidence gating

Priyom / Ben —

A few internal alignment notes before we hand artifacts over:
- Ben, can you own collection for SOC 2 config snapshots and access-review exports (owner: ben_carter). Expectation: redacted CSV exports showing reviewers and timestamps.
- Priyom, you'll continue to coordinate ISO/Scope artifacts and the SIG crosswalk (owner: priyom_das).
- I will handle any KMS/keyproof escalations and provide a templated JSON sample proving rotation and CMK access provenance.

Flag: Highland asked for telemetry evidence; we should push a short README explaining how telemetry is sampled for third-party review (to avoid sending raw production logs). Suggest we provide: a telemetry runbook excerpt + prefiltered sample data accompanied by a redaction summary.

Schedule: I can join the kickoff call to answer any KMS/provenance questions. If Highland requests an on-prem walkthrough for encryption controls we can replicate the environment with sanitized examples.

Kimberly Park
Security Program Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@highlandcap.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Highland Capital RFP — SIG/ISO evidence lane and upload cadence

Anya / team —

Thanks for the clarity, Anya. Per Priyom's Phase 1 commitments, we've flagged the following deliverables for upload within 10 business days:
- SIG control crosswalk (CSV + narrative)
- ISO scope map (pdf)
- KMS rotation sample (redacted JSON)
- Access review export (redacted CSV)
- Telemetry runbook excerpt + pre-filtered sample (sanitized)

A few clarifying asks for Highland to confirm:
1) Are screenshots acceptable in-lieu of live console exports for items that contain PII?
2) For KMS proofs, do you require HSM attestation or is Cloud KMS rotation logs sufficient for initial validation?

Can we confirm: presigned S3 with 72-hour TTL is acceptable? If you need 7-day TTL, we can extend but prefer to keep short-lived links for security.

I'll upload the crosswalk and the access export first as a canary set so your team can verify format. Expect the first presigned URL by EOD PT today.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Assurance Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachment references: SIG_artifact_worksheet_v1.xlsx (owners column updated)
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@highlandcap.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@highlandcap.com
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Highland Capital RFP — SIG/ISO evidence lane and upload cadence

Ben / Priyom —

Thanks — that approach works. Quick answers:
- Screenshots are acceptable for sensitive configs so long as they include timestamps and user IDs; attach a short attestation stating the scope of redaction.
- For initial validation, Cloud KMS rotation logs are sufficient. We will request HSM attestation only if we find a control gap that requires deeper proof.
- 72-hour presigned TTL is fine; if we hit long-running uploads we'll request extensions case-by-case.

We confirm the kickoff call tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT. Procurement will use the HubSpot deal number HC-2029-RFP-007 to track the artifacts.

Anya
Head of Vendor Assurance — Highland Capital
